cycleNewer.label: Fall 2026 entering class (Class of 2030)
cycleNewer.doc: WashU Office of Undergraduate Admissions, Class of 2030 Profile (numbers accurate as of September 21, 2026; 'enrolling' count)

scores.doc: Class of 2030 Profile: middle 50% SAT 1510-1550, ACT 33-35; 63% enrolled with test scores, 37% without (no split between SAT and ACT, no medians)

testPolicy.text: WashU is test optional. Applicants who choose to submit scores may self-report them on the Common App or Coalition App; enrolling students who submitted unofficial scores must then send official score reports. Either SAT or ACT; writing not required; ACT science optional.

gpa.doc: No Common Data Set published; the class profile gives no GPA (88% of students reporting rank were in the top 10% of their class)

cost.totalIncludes: university charges 96,994 (tuition 71,310 + student activity fee 712 + student health and wellness fee 700 + average housing and food 24,272, modern double and Platinum meal plan) + other estimated expenses 5,266 (books and supplies 1,412 + travel 1,050 + miscellaneous 2,804). The total 102,260 is the sum of the two subtotals WashU publishes.

aidPromise.text: WashU meets 100% of demonstrated need without loans (no-loan policy) for all admitted students. Admission is need-blind for first-year U.S. citizen and permanent resident applicants (not for international, transfer or waitlist admits). The WashU Pledge gives a free education (tuition, fees, housing and food, guaranteed four years) to incoming full-time students from Missouri or 53 southern Illinois counties with family income of $75,000 or less.

deadlines.early: November 2 (Early Action, decisions by December 23; Early Decision I, decisions by December 11); Early Decision II January 4 (decisions by February 12)

facts.text: For fall 2027 applicants WashU has added a non-binding Early Action round (November 2) alongside Early Decision I (November 2), Early Decision II (January 4) and Regular Decision (January 4).
For the Class of 2030 (fall 2026), 4,057 of 33,214 applicants were admitted (12%) and 1,941 are enrolling, 1,330 of them in Arts and Sciences and 300 in Engineering.
Missouri and southern Illinois students from families earning $75,000 or less attend free under the WashU Pledge, covering tuition, fees, housing and food for four years.

School scholarships and Signature Scholar Programs are awarded after the Early Decision II notification date, so WashU recommends Regular Decision for students who need an academic scholarship to attend; priority scholarship applications are due December 16.
37% of the Class of 2030 enrolled without submitting test scores.
University charges for 2026-27 total $96,994, and $102,260 with estimated books, travel and personal costs.

notes: WashU does not publish a Common Data Set on any page reached (provost Institutional Research and Institutional Effectiveness pages list no CDS; irads.wustl.edu does not resolve). No fall 2025 (Class of 2029) official profile is online any more: the admissions profile page now shows the Class of 2030. So 'cycle' is null and the newest official numbers are in 'cycleNewer' (enrolling count as of 2026-09-21, not a final census). Archive services were not used. Score medians, SAT/ACT split, section scores and GPA are not published. cost.fees = 712 + 700 = 1,412 (the same amount as books and supplies, by coincidence).
